claim: *The engineering modeling repertoire.* Familiar representations preserve different relationships for different engineering questions. Similar graphical forms can carry different semantics: an arrow may represent a dependency, transition, flow, permission, ownership relation, or derivation.

topology.description: Restored visible node boxes in all nine miniature model forms and the quantitative bound bracket. Preserved each actual graph, forbidden/stale crosses and dashed edges, source questions/properties/analyses, and three-column hierarchy.

required_terms: Q = question · P = property · A = analysis
bw_encoding: Nine equal white panels and all miniature nodes white. Shape, topology, labels and dashed/cross marks distinguish forms.
redesign: Nine equal white panels and all miniature nodes white. Shape, topology, labels and dashed/cross marks distinguish forms. All miniature process/relation edges use aligned ports and short orthogonal branches; forbidden/stale crosses follow their dashed paths.
alt: Nine miniature graphs in a three-by-three grid show component dependencies, finite states, data flow, ownership, policy decisions, quantitative bounds, entity schemas, provenance and call flow. Every form has its own question, properties and analyses. Dashed crossed edges mark stale or prohibited relations; a bracket marks the quantitative bound.
